tldr: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI was reported on Oct 5 to be preparing a "DeepSeek of the West" open model. Beam, a 501B-parameter model with 23B active, shipped Oct 6 and was framed against low-cost Chinese models.
whats_new: On Oct 16, AWS published a SageMaker deployment guide for Beam and vLLM shipped day-0 serving, so the 501B-A23B model now runs on both a managed endpoint and an open inference stack.
why_it_matters: Beam can now be tested on a SageMaker JumpStart endpoint or your own vLLM stack; the reported Nvidia acquisition bid still leaves its license and release cadence unsettled.

beats.headline: Nvidia-backed Reflection preps an open model, framed as a DeepSeek of the West
Beam (501B-A23B) released as an American open model
Coverage turns to Beam's position against low-cost Chinese models
Report: Nvidia pursues acquisition of Reflection to counter DeepSeek
vLLM and AWS add Beam-1.0 deployment paths
beats.summary: vLLM reports a 2.71× decode-latency cut from agent-driven optimization and DFlash2 speculative decoding; AWS documents a SageMaker JumpStart real-time endpoint.

open_questions: How does Beam score against DeepSeek and Kimi on independent evals?
What license and per-token inference cost does Beam ship with on SageMaker and elsewhere?
Does Nvidia confirm an acquisition, and does Beam's open-weight license change?
Does the 2.71× vLLM decode speedup hold on hardware outside vLLM's own test setup?
take_for_builders: Run Beam on vLLM or a SageMaker JumpStart endpoint against your open-weight eval shortlist, and pin the exact weights and license text you test until the ownership question is settled.
